text.p: Following are some of the leading stories in the Swedish papers this morning. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Hundreds of people are left isolated in northern Sweden following flooding in parts of Norrbotten and Vasterbotten. More rain is expected in these areas.

- A new proposal could allow the state-owned postal service to lower postage rates for local post to meet competition from local post companies. Local post accounts for about 15 percent of the total received.

- Drugs company Pharmacia & Upjohn posted a worse than expected result for the second quarter of 1997. The result, with a profit 33 percent lower than a year ago, again shows that the 1995 merger of Sweden's Pharmacia and the U.S. Upjohn has yet to prove its worth.

- The joint venture ferry company to be formed by Sweden's Stena Line and Britain's P&O on the English Channel will miss the high season this summer. Approvals from both the British Government and the European Union are late.

- Sweden's population has only increased by about 5,000 over the past year which is the lowest level since 1983. This year the number of babies to be born per woman is expected to be lower than ever before.
- Swedish home furnishings retailer IKEA is hoping for a bout of nasty weather when it releases its new catalogue in two weeks time. Sales slip when the weather is good.

- U.S./Swedish drugs company Pharmacia & Upjohn posted dramatically lower profits for the first half of 1997. After non recurring costs earnings fell 25 percent. Chief executive Fred Hassan said the negative trends were continuing but expected a turnaround in 1998. The share price fell on the report but recovered later on Tuesday.

- Elanders purchase of Skandinaviska Lithorex will form the Nordic area's leading company for direct advertising. Elanders Lithorex AB, which will be included in Elanders' advertising business area, will be headed by Havard Grjotheim who expects to see profits by 1998.

- The Swedish government is witnessing a public revolt against tax increases with consumption of petrol, oil, spirits and tobacco falling as taxes are pushed up. The increase in sales of beer and company cars on which taxes have been lowered have been less than the falls.
- Drugs company Pharmacia & Upjohn's problems in the first half of 1997 are set to continue. Its pre-tax profit in the first half rose to $564 million from $197 million a year ago but sales fell.
- Shipping group Bylock & Nordsjofrakt have bought three new icebreakers in cooperation with Norway's offshore company Viking Supply Ships AS worth an estimated one billion crowns.
